entries.problem: Classical sample-variance empirical Bernstein requires i.i.d. data, while the common-conditional-mean predictable-plug-in theorem permits non-i.i.d. laws only when their conditional means are equal. Neither premise is identical to R163's independent, possibly unequal finite-design means.
entries.effective_correction: Use R164's constant-bet average-conditional-mean theorem. Under independent participants it targets the exact unweighted R163 finite-design mean. Varying-bet methods require a separate unweighted-target proof or an explicitly weighted estimand.
entries.downstream_rule_effect: No inherited rule is deleted. R164 adds an alternative exact planwise discharge. R163 Hoeffding remains the range-only fallback and the R162 tower theorem remains unchanged.
